item.title: Patrick Stewart, best known for "Star Trek" and "X-Men," dies at 86
item.description: Patrick Stewart starred on stage and screen across his decadeslong acting career. He died at his home on Wednesday.

item.title: Iran claims 4 tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: A tanker was also struck by a projectile in the strait on Thursday night.

item.title: Millions of French press coffee makers recalled due to burn risk
item.description: Product safety regulators said the glass carafes can unexpectedly break if they are damaged or cracked, leading to burn injuries.

item.title: From the archives: Patrick Stewart on "Star Trek" and Shakespeare
item.description: Sir Patrick Stewart, the classically-trained stage actor who was best-known for his roles in the "Star Trek" and "X-Men" franchises, died on Oct. 28, 2026 at age 86. In this "Sunday Morning" profile that aired May 24, 2020, Stewart talked with CBS News' Tony Dokoupil about returning to the role of Captain Jean Luc Picard in the TV series "Star Trek: Picard," and about how he sought an escape from the COVID pandemic through the Bard's poetry.

item.title: What to know about Alaska's Senate race as ballot fight heats up
item.description: In Alaska's Senate race, voters will choose between four candidates, including GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan and a man with the same first and last name — a situation that has frustrated Republicans and drawn scrutiny for Democrat Mary Peltola.

item.title: How debates became high-risk and low-reward in the viral era
item.description: Half of the Senate and a third of gubernatorial races will go without a debate between major party candidates in the 2026 cycle.

item.title: Legendary actor Patrick Stewart dies at 86
item.description: Beloved "Star Trek" and "X-Men" actor Sir Patrick Stewart has died at 86 following a battle with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, his representatives said.

item.title: Guilty plea on federal charges in deadly Boulder firebomb attack
item.description: The man who already pleaded guilty to more than 100 state criminal charges, including first-degree murder, for an attack on the Pearl Street Mall in June 2025, appeared in federal court on Thursday where he changed his plea to guilty on a dozen charges.

item.title: Midterm elections put Social Security funding gaps on the ballot
item.description: With Social Security's main trust fund on course to be depleted in 2032, Congress will face mounting pressure to find remedies and avert benefit cuts.

item.title: AI deepfakes pose risks to consumers and voters, experts warn
item.description: "When you can't tell what's legitimate, you question everything," said one cybersecurity expert focused on political campaigns.

item.title: DOJ vets say politically charged moves close to election violate norms
item.description: Former DOJ officials say Attorney General Todd Blanche's Justice Department has entered uncharted waters in ways that could influence politics.

item.title: Spacewalkers begin final phase of a space station upgrade
item.description: Two astronauts stepped outside the International Space Station for the first of two spacewalks, one week apart, to complete a complex upgrade to the aging power system.

item.title: Live Updates: Trump campaigns in South Carolina and more
item.description: More than 42 million Americans had voted early as of Thursday afternoon, according to the University of Florida Election Lab.

item.title: Maps and charts show record number of measles cases in U.S. this year
item.description: CBS News has been tracking a record number of measles cases and outbreaks around the country in 2026. The majority of cases are among those who haven't been vaccinated.

item.title: No clear winner in Israeli election as negotiations to follow
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party won more votes than his main challenger, but both sides will likely struggle to cobble together a coalition.

item.title: Michigan Senate race between El Sayed, Rogers remains a toss-up as candidates make final push
item.description: The Michigan Senate race remains a toss-up between Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers. Meanwhile, the New Hampshire Senate race heated up between candidates Chris Pappas and John Sununu during a Wednesday night debate. CBS News' Kaia Hubbard has more.

item.title: Finnish diplomat on Putin's rare phone call with leaders of Finland, Norway over Ukraine war
item.description: The leaders of Finland and Norway discussed the war in Ukraine in a rare phone call with Russia's Vladimir Putin. Finnish foreign minister Elina Valtonen shares her thoughts.

item.title: Trump says two Dan Sullivans on Alaska Senate ballot is "very unfair"
item.description: President Trump spoke to reporters before leaving for a South Carolina rally, where he weighed in on the Alaska Senate race featuring two Dan Sullivans.

item.title: Cruise ship passengers wanted a yearslong dream trip. Now the trip is canceled due to fuel costs.
item.description: An American cruise ship suspended a three-year global voyage in Cambodia due to high fuel costs. Now passengers who planned to live at sea, many of them retirees, must cope with disrupted plans and finances. CBS News' Cristian Benavides has more on this story.

item.title: Election law expert on 2 Dan Sullivans in Alaska, DOJ bid to force California to set aside ballots
item.description: Alaska's Republican governor is calling for an investigation into an alleged ballot-stacking scheme by putting two Dan Sullivans on the ticket. CBS News' Taurean Small reports, and election expert and contributor David Becker joins to discuss.

item.title: Watch: Mike Waltz gets into shouting match with Cuban delegation on U.N. floor
item.description: U.S. ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz got into a shouting match with the Cuban delegation while speaking at the United Nations.

item.title: U.S. citizens included on DOJ list of 400 alleged noncitizens, Washington says
item.description: Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs told two federal prosecutors that "many" U.S. citizens were included on a Justice Department list of suspected noncitizens.

item.title: Russian strikes kill 14 in Ukraine but local truce brings some hope
item.description: A Russian drone hit two trains at a station in central Ukraine, killing at least 14 people, but a local truce credited to Melania Trump is bringing some hope elsewhere.

item.title: Items found in Pompeii home hint at life before volcanic explosion
item.description: Coins, jewelry and other artifacts were found in a sealed closet in Pompeii, giving new insight into life in the historic Roman city before it was destroyed in A.D. 79.

item.title: King faces calls for apology, slavery reparations in Caribbean
item.description: King Charles III faces renewed calls for a slavery apology and reparations on a visit to the Caribbean, as protesters demand: "Pay us what you owe us."

item.title: DoorDash gobbles up Instacart in $17 billion deal
item.description: DoorDash's purchase of Instacart for $65 per share will unite two of the country's largest grocery and food-delivery companies.

item.title: Hegseth fires Pentagon's top military planner over alleged leaks
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired the Pentagon's top military planner, Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, a Pentagon official told CBS News.

item.title: How to watch live 2026 election results on CBS News
item.description: With control of Congress on the line in House and Senate races around the country, here's how to watch the 2026 midterm election results on Tuesday, Nov. 3.

item.title: California high-speed rail consultants billed taxpayers for late-night rides from CEO's home
item.description: CBS California Investigates obtained receipts behind the watchdog's findings of wasteful spending, revealing previously undisclosed connections to the high-speed rail CEO.

item.title: Sir Patrick Stewart on "Star Trek" and sonnets
item.description: The Shakespearean actor most recognized for his performances in the sci-fi franchises "X-Men" and "Star Trek" talks about playing Captain Jean Luc Picard, and how he sought an escape from the pandemic through poetry
